doubts: (a) Main alternative: NO_ACTION (POL-GEN-03 party-relative) - treat the driver's traffic excuse as weightless under POL-RD-08/POL-RD-13(2) because the advisory is MISSING, the deviation is established on a clean trace, and the 6.05 already refunded equals the POL-RD-02 figure, so the rider stays refunded. That reading ignores POL-RD-13's express carve-out that a party who cites the missing identifier still escalates under POL-RD-10(5), so I reject it, but a reviewer weighting the human-closure rationale (absent advisory = weightless excuse) heavily might land there. (b) POL-RD-13 is written with a rider-filed posture in mind ('where the rider has shown an excess'); here the driver files and the rider is already refunded, but the POL-RD-10(5) trigger is posture-neutral. (c) The driver says the 'dispute page show' the advisory, so the cited ID was platform-minted rather than invented by the driver; that does not change the analysis - the artifact is still missing and cited. (d) If the advisory were later produced and covered PIE near Kallang in the window, POL-RD-03 would exonerate up to min(5.08, 1.30 x (alt - 12.8) + 1.00), possibly a FULL_REFUND (6.05) or PARTIAL_REFUND to the driver; that cannot be computed without shortest_lawful_alternative_km.
